The Kibo Project — The more I try to write about this place, the more I feel words fall short.
I came across this medical centre very recently when a small pup, Lisa, met with a road accident. We rushed her there and were told that she would need complete cage rest and medical attention for around 15 days. At first, I was hesitant and anxious. But today, after a week, I can proudly say that every one of my worries has been proven wrong, thanks to Ankita and the incredible team there (I’m sorry I don’t know everyone’s names). They have been taking such wonderful care of Lisa and giving her all the medical attention she needs. The improvement in her condition is already visible.
And it’s not just Lisa — the entire team looks after all the doggos and cattos there with so much love and dedication. I’ve honestly never seen such a clean and hygienic centre before. Everyone works tirelessly, round the clock, for the little world they have built for these animals.
Lisa has also made some adorable friends there — Bittey, Motor, Sarah, and Blackcurrant ❤️
Thank you so much to all of you, and kudos for the incredible work you’re doing. Much love!!!

featured_reviews.name: Rita Varma
featured_reviews.review_text:
I trusted Kibo with my cat, Chittu, for a few days of fluid therapy and oral medication, and it turned out to be one of the worst decisions I’ve made. I had heard good things about them, but my experience was nothing short of traumatic.

Throughout Chittu’s stay, getting updates was incredibly difficult. They only sent pictures after I repeatedly asked, and even those updates didn’t reflect the reality of what my baby was going through. A couple of days later, I noticed bruising in one of the photos, which made me feel something was seriously wrong so I went to pick him up.

What I saw broke me.
My cat had bruises in multiple places, even around the neck. He smelled strongly of urine, as if he had been left lying in it. His fur and skin were in terrible condition, and he was severely dehydrated. The updates they gave me were completely misleading compared to his actual state.

I had provided all his oral medications, yet they were returned to me unopened. This means none of his medications were given, which could have significantly contributed to his decline. His IV catheter wasn’t changed for days, causing phlebitis and bruising at the site, something that no responsible clinic should overlook.

Because of the condition Chittu was in when I brought him home, I was forced to make the heartbreaking decision of putting him to sleep. I cannot express the pain of knowing my baby could have had more time and comfort, but that chance was taken away from him.

Although I understood that my pet’s blood values didn’t indicate a good prognosis, I still believed he deserved every possible chance at recovery. Working in the medical field myself, I’ve seen many patients improve when the right line of treatment is followed. As a pet parent, my only wish was for him to receive proper care, comfort, and hygiene especially towards the end of his life.

Unfortunately, Kibo failed to provide even that basic dignity. What should have been compassionate, attentive care turned into a deeply disappointing and hurtful experience.

I trusted Kibo, and they failed my baby in every possible way. I will never forgive the negligence and lack of basic care that cost my cat his remaining time. I would not recommend this place to anyone who loves their pet.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Edit 23.11 1845 hrs: After our response to the review, you have posted misleading photographs, which we are constrained to clarify - As mentioned below, Chittu was on IV for 9 hours a day. This will in most cases lead to inflammation of the area where the catheter is inserted (known as thrombo-phlebitis), a common offshoot and not at all a significant medical issue or fatal to say the least. Unfortunately Google does not let us post photos as the business owner, we have sent them to you on WA.

Dear Rita

It is very unfortunate that you had a bad experience with us. We put our heart and soul into the work we do, and your feedback has deeply affected us.

We have an 'open-door' policy for all clients and you did not once raise any of these issues you are now highlighting at any point when Chittu was admitted with us. We would therefore like to clear the air on some of the issues you have raised:

1. Chittu was admitted with us on 29.10.25. His creatine levels were very high and he had totally stopped eating. He was also very dehydrated and was advised renal wet food, which you provided. We used the food you provided.

2. As per the primary vet's prescription (in your case - Crown Vets), we administered slow IV fluid therapy for 9 hours everyday, along with antibiotics and oral medication. We used the medicines available in our existing inventory (since these were already opened), and therefore did not use the fresh batch of the drugs you provided, which was duly returned to you unused and unopened.

3. Pursuant to the treatment administered, Chittu began eating slowly (chicken liver) and showed some signs of improvement. We gave you regular and daily updates on WhatsApp with pictures, status of his food intake etc. After your review, we have also forwarded screenshots of all updates to your WhatsApp number again.

4. However, on 08.11.25 (9th day at Kibo), Chittu was looking dull and had stopped eating. We promptly informed you, and you came and took him from the centre to get him checked with the primary vet. Chittu was cleaned, put in a clean basket and handed over to you. Pictures of the cat were also shared with you as per our protocol. There was no bruising whatsoever, and it is completely not true that you came to pick up Chittu because of bruising, that is simply not true.

5. Less than 2 hours later, you informed us that Chittu was no more. You also informed us that you come the following day to pick up the unused medicines which you would use for your other rescues/ community cats.

We were not aware until this review that Chittu was put to sleep. At the time we handed the cat over to you, Chittu was not discharged from Kibo and you took him for a checkup since his condition was deteriorating. In fact, until this review, you had never even raised a single grievance with us, all of which is borne from our chats with you.

It is therefore quite shocking to note your feedback, which is completely contrary to what has transpired. Chittu certainly deserved every chance of recovery and we have provided him that to the best of the medical advice given by the primary vet.

We are all part of the community working for the betterment of animals. We are all human, and to err is human. At Kibo, we have a strong policy of admitting that we have made a mistake if that were the case. Because from that mistake comes a much bigger learning. But this is simply not the case here, it is very unfortunate you have this feedback. 

We have also tried contacting you multiple times but have not been able to get through. We remain available to discuss anything further on this should you require.

Regards
Team Kibo

🐈 Flight of Pheonix 🐈

I found a this ginger kitten near Phoenix Mall, Kurla, in a very critical condition. He was barely able to walk, covered in flies, and refusing to eat. I reached out to several animal NGOs, but no one responded or picked up my calls.
Then I called Kibo Project, and to my relief, they immediately picked up and accepted the cat. I honestly didn’t think he would make it, but the Kibo team Riya, Abhishek, Vaibhav and Dr. Atharva showed incredible dedication. They kept me updated daily with photos and health reports of the kitten, whom I named Phoenix after the mall.
Over the next 18 days, I visited them a few times and even brought food for all the cats at their shelter. I’m so grateful that Phoenix fully recovered, was vaccinated and dewormed, and was released back near the mall yesterday, 3rd December.
The entire team’s commitment made all the difference. Thank you to Pragya for founding such an essential NGO. This world needs more people like you. I will always be thankful to Kibo Project for giving Phoenix a second chance at life.

Adapting to Change in Dynamic Business Environments

A pace where Gen Z is redefining expectations, millennials are trying to keep up and Gen X is learning to stay afloat. Change is no longer an event. It is the environment. And it calls for all of us to cultivate an adaptive mindset.

Adaptation requires a deliberate and conscious shift. It means encouraging continuous learning, making faster decisions with imperfect information and creating a culture where experimentation feels safe, not scary.

Leaders need to move from control to clarity. While setting direction, they must empower teams, involve them in the change process and address concerns to reduce resistance. The real edge lies in staying curious, aligning quickly, and treating change as fuel.

Successful organizations are those that adapt quickly, empower their people and build resilient, future ready teams.

At The Yellow Spot, we help leaders and teams navigate uncertainty with clarity, confidence and agility. From mindset shifts to actionable strategies, we enable real transformation that sticks.

Ready to lead change instead of reacting to it? Let’s build your competitive edge.

How to Improve Management Skills Across Teams

The golden rule of good management is clarity and consistency. . 
The team that works with clear goals is a happy and successful one. A good manager will align these goals with the organization’s larger vision to create purpose-driven work.  Here, communication is the biggest lever. Ensure you do regular check-ins with your team. Give them transparent feedback and listen to them actively. Ask them for their feedback. This builds trust and reduces friction.
Next, focus on empowering your people. Delegate with intention, not just to offload work but to develop ownership and leadership within the team. Great managers coach more than they control.
Standardizing processes across teams can also eliminate confusion and boost efficiency. However, leave room for flexibility. What works for one team might not work for another.
Invest in continuous learning. Workshops, leadership training and peer learning groups help managers stay sharp and adaptable in a fast-changing work environment.
Finally, track progress. Use simple metrics like team engagement, productivity and feedback scores to understand what’s working and what’s not.
Improving management skills is an ongoing journey and not a one-time activity. When done right it builds high-performing, motivated teams that deliver consistent results.

If you are looking to sharpen your management skills, call or write to us

Importance of Communication and Feedback Skills in Performance Management

It's that time of the year that concerns everyone — leaders, managers, team members and HR alike.
It's performance appraisal time. Rating time. Time to implement the bell curve and review the OKRs.

And the one skill that proves most handy is, the way performance is communicated and feedback is given and received across all levels.

While some leaders and managers practice naturally, for most, it needs to be learned and practiced.

•	Preparation before the conversation — past records, notes, emails, work-related data, appreciations, errors and behaviour with colleagues.
•	The external environment — the right meeting space, no phones, no interruptions and a comfortable seating arrangement.

Build a Safe Compliant and Respectful Workplace with POSH Training
POSH (Prevention of Sexual Harassment) training in Indian workplaces is mandated under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013. Every organization is required to create awareness, prevent misconduct and provide a safe redressal system.
When done right POSH training goes far beyond compliance. For organizations it reduces legal risk, protects reputation and strengthens a culture of trust and accountability. For employees it builds clarity on acceptable behaviour, encourages confidence to speak up and creates a sense of safety at work.
Not all POSH training is the same. It can include awareness sessions for employees, capacity building for managers and specialized workshops for Internal Committee members who handle cases. Each level plays a critical role in making the system effective.
At The Yellow Spot we focus on making POSH training practical, relevant and engaging. Through real workplace scenarios interactive discussions and simple frameworks, we help teams not just understand the law but apply it in everyday interactions.
A safe workplace does not happen by chance. It is built with intent and consistency.

Emotional Intelligence for Leadership and Team Effectiveness.

For centuries humans have valued intelligence. It is something we all admire, pursue and expect in ourselves and others. From academic success to professional growth, intelligence has always been seen as a key driver of achievement.
This is slowly shifting. 
Emotional Intelligence has become a must have for Leadership and Team Effectiveness.
Time has always taught us how crucial it is to understand, manage and connect with people.
Leaders with strong emotional intelligence do just that. They
✔ Communicate with clarity and empathy
✔ Handle conflict without damaging relationships
✔ Build trust that drives collaboration
✔ Stay composed under pressure
✔ Inspire accountability, not fear
And that’s where the real impact is seen.
Under such leaders the whole organisation grows stronger and more resilient as communication becomes clearer, engagement rises and teams are aligned towards the ultimate goal. 
So, if your leaders are technically strong but struggling to connect, influence or drive team effectiveness, it’s time to build Emotional Intelligence where it matters most.
Ready to strengthen your leadership and unlock team performance? At The Yellow Spot, we help leaders and teams unlock performance through practical, high-impact Emotional Intelligence training.

Call us today or message us to design a customized Emotional Intelligence program for you.

Leadership Communication During Change in Mumbai

I often hear leaders say, “Things are changing faster than we can explain them to our teams.”
Change has become the new constant. In a fast-paced city like Mumbai, it feels even more intense. We are dealing with tight deadlines, sky high expectations and constant movement. 
In such an environment, leadership communication is what keeps teams together and going. People today are not just looking for direction, they are looking for clarity, reassurance and trust.
We come across leaders focusing only on what is changing. The real impact, however, lies in how the change is communicated.
Simply announcing a new process or restructuring is not enough. Teams need to understand why the change is happening, how it will affect them and what is expected from them going forward. Ambiguity creates a lot of panic as people tend to assume the worst. 
So here is what a good leader should ensure:
• Clarity – What is changing and why
• Consistency – Keeping messages aligned across levels
• Empathy – Acknowledging concerns and resistance
• Visibility – Being available and approachable
When leaders communicate well, uncertainty reduces, alignment improves and teams move forward with greater confidence.
If you are looking to support your leaders in managing communication during change, we can help. We conduct training programmes focused on building practical, real-world leadership communication skills. Connect with us to know more.

Ownership and Accountability in High-Performance Teams

We’ve been receiving a lot of enquiries for ownership and accountability trainings lately. And honestly, that’s a great sign.
Organisations are starting to realise that results don’t come from just the leader pushing things through. In fact, it actually works the best when everyone in the team takes responsibility.
When everyone knows exactly what they have to do, feel strongly about it and go all out to get it done, things move much faster and better. That’s ownership.
And accountability? When something goes wrong, instead of blaming others, you accept it and quickly move towards finding and implementing a solution.
While its mainly about a mindset shift (and occasionally about the style of the leader), a few simple tools can really help.
One such tool is the RACI Matrix. It’s a popular project management tool which helps teams complete tasks more effectively by enhancing clarity on who will be playing which role during completion of each task. 
•	Responsible - Who is supposed to complete the task  
•	Accountable - Who has the final responsibility of completing the task
•	Consulted - Who’s inputs are to be taken to complete the task effectively
•	Informed - Which stakeholders are to be kept in the loop on the task status
If you are looking at supporting your team in taking more ownership, we are here to help. We conduct trainings that help enhance ownership and accountability of teams. Connect with us to know more.

Design Thinking Training for Innovation and Problem Solving

Have you ever felt your current problem-solving tools lacked something important? That they were a little lop-sided. More focused on logic and analysis and often missed out on the human and emotional aspect.  

Now that’s where Design Thinking comes in. A popular tool used extensively by organisations nowadays for a huge variety of uses. From solving complex problems, enhancing customer experience to even creating the next innovation. Design Thinking has got it all. It helps teams look at problems from the user’s point of view and find solutions that actually work. Its a practical yet human-centred approach that gives you the best for both worlds and offers a more holistic approach to problem solving. 

The process is as follows: 
1.	Empathize – Get deep into what the user really wants and needs
2.	Define – State the problem and objective in simple terms
3.	Ideate – Challenge what exists and generate new ideas
4.	Protype – Come up with possible solutions
5.	Test – Experiment to check the feasibility of the solution

Design Thinking helps teams think differently. It focuses on identifying real pain points, bringing people together to explore fresh perspectives and testing ideas to see what truly works.

Inquisitive to know more about Design Thinking and how it can help your team? Connect with us. We would be happy to conduct a tailor-made Design Thinking Training for your organisation.

featured_reviews.name: Saurabh Gupta
featured_reviews.review_text:
I kept my dog Shadow at Pawfect Life for 2 nights and 2 days because I was going on travel. I chose this place because the reviews looked decent and the pricing was on the cheaper side. But honestly, the experience was very odd.

When I brought Shadow back home, he was smelling really bad like full-on urine. The smell was so strong that my entire living room started smelling. It literally took me almost 3 days of proper cleaning and disinfecting Shadow with betadine solution to get the smell out of him. That clearly shows there’s a serious hygiene issue at the facility.

Agreed, it’s affordable, but it feels like hygiene and cleanliness are being compromised because of that. If you’re keeping multiple dogs, you need enough staff, regular cleaning, and proper care. Unfortunately that didn’t seem to be case, at least in my experience.

For this reason I started doing more research asking others about recommendations and experiences. While talking to another dog owner at the Hiranandani Powai dog park, she told me her husky had stayed here earlier and was bitten by another dog. Her dog’s ear was injured badly and had to be stitched.

The shocking part was they got the stitching done without informing her or taking her permission, even though she was travelling. She “discovered” the stitches only when her husky was dropped back to her home. When she called them she came to know about he fact they had stitched her ear without informing her and without her permission. Is that even ethical?
The two stars I have given is because they have affordable pricing and pick and drop facility (at a price).

I’d be very careful before leaving the dog here. Until hygiene, safety, supervision, and communication improve, I personally wouldn’t feel comfortable boarding my dog again. Pets deserve better care, not just cheap boarding.

featured_reviews.review_text: I had few cats neutered with this NGO. Good thing is that they are good at surgery. Bad thing. The staff never picks up call or responds to your concerns about the cat. As a caretaker, we are concerned for our cats health especially if they are at a new place. As an NGO they should understand and inculcate in this behaviour. Swapna is too rude and arrogant. She should improve her behaviour and talking skills with people. You are not doing any favour on your customers. In facts customer favours you. This attitude won’t go long way. featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Dear Vishnu Priya

Thank you for your feedback and appreciating our work. However we would like to clarify a few points regarding your visit. 

Our centre functions by prior appointment, especially for surgeries. Despite knowing this you brought a cat for spay without an appointment. We understand the difficulty of trapping community cats and hence accepted your cat for spay. 

You expected our staff to clean your soiled crate. During peak surgical hours, our staff is occupied in surgeries, post-op and medical care. We cannot divert our staff’s medical time to clean personal transport crates. This was not rudeness, but a matter of clinical responsibility and hygiene protocol.

We appreciate individuals who bring community cats for sterilisation; however, this is not a favour to the organisation. This is a collaborative welfare effort that requires mutual respect.

We stand by our team’s professionalism and commitment to animal welfare.

Team All About Them

featured_reviews.name: Mohsin Qureshi
featured_reviews.review_text:
I took my cat, Panda, to All About Them for neutering. She was a tuxedo cat. I was charged ₹2,500 for the procedure, which included post-operative care. However, when I brought her home after she stayed at their clinic for two days following the surgery, she seemed extremely lethargic.

Fifteen days after bringing her back, she suddenly fell very ill and had difficulty walking. I rushed her to the hospital, where the vet mentioned that she might have contracted a viral infection from being in a place with many other cats. When I informed the doctor that she had been neutered and had stayed at All About Them for two days, he confirmed that it was possible she had picked up the infection there.

Unfortunately, despite receiving multiple injections and fluids, she couldn’t recover and sadly passed away the same day. I don’t directly blame All About Them, but I am deeply disappointed because they assured me that the cats would be well cared for during post-op recovery. Had I known that infections were a risk at their facility, I would have taken her home immediately after the surgery instead.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Dear Mohsin we are extremely sorry for the loss of your pet but it is unfortunate to know about this incident over a review.

We were never informed post the discharge that the cat had fallen ill. We have operated over 24000 cats and have always taken accountability for any complication that might occur.

Since it is a pet, it is advised to vaccinate before any surgery as in NGO the influx of  community animals is vey high.

If you have any further doubts please feel free to reach us.

featured_reviews.name: D Joseph
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Heartfelt Thank You to TATF & Deepa

As many of our friends know, 2023 didn’t end gently for us. It was a time filled with grief, long days, and sleepless nights.

But in that silence, we realized we might need someone to help us through.

Not something impulsive, not a rushed decision, just an unspoken understanding between the two of us that perhaps the love we had to give wasn’t meant to stop.

And that’s when fate stepped in.

While scrolling through Instagram one night, I came across The Anubis-Tiger Foundation. Something nudged me to send a message, just putting it out there that we were open to welcoming a pup in need of a home.

I didn’t expect a reply so soon. But within a few hours, Deepa reached out - with a photo of an angel who, as it turned out, was waiting for us too.

The moment we saw her, we just knew.
She was ours. And we were hers.

Despite everything, I never imagined it would all happen so quickly. But perhaps that’s because I hadn’t realized just how many people are out there giving up their pets, sometimes for heartbreaking reasons. It left me sad, confused, and questioning how anyone could let go of such love.

But I’ll be honest - we’re also thankful.

Because if that family hadn’t made their decision, we would’ve never met Aura.

On 21st January 2024, we brought her home. We braced ourselves, thinking she might take time to adjust after a year with her previous family.

But Aura had other plans.

Within a day, she chose us - just as we had chosen her. She knew she was home.

She changed everything. The energy, the silence, the air itself. And her name came so naturally: Aura.

We went into this thinking we were rescuing her. But in truth, she rescued us.

We are so grateful to have her in our lives.

Thank you, Deepa, you who don’t just find homes for these beautiful souls, but make sure they find the right ones.

She doesn’t hand them over to just anyone. She takes the time to check, to understand, and to ensure that the home is one filled with the love, care, and stability every animal deserves.

Thank you, Anubis Foundation.
And thank you to the angel above who showed us the way.

❤️

I contacted this rescue because they were the closest to my location—just a 17-minute ride away. I called them multiple times, and my dad also personally called and spoke to them. We were assured that something would be done.

The first call was made at 1:08 PM. It is now 4:50 PM, and there has been absolutely no response or sign of help. We waited for hours, hoping for a reply. Sadly, the dog is no longer breathing.

This kind of negligence is unacceptable from an organization that claims to rescue animals. Because of this experience, we will be leaving very negative reviews and strongly urge others to reconsider relying on this service in emergencies.
